title: AI Red Teaming Agent — Extended Skills Curriculum

skills.title: Web application and API security
skills.purpose: Understand and assess the web/API layer that exposes AI functionality; identify whether security failures are in the model, application, identity layer or backend.
safe_labs: Build a local FastAPI service with login, a read-only search endpoint and a mock write endpoint. Test authentication and object-level authorization using two synthetic users.
Use Burp Suite or OWASP ZAP against the local app to inspect requests, sessions, headers, API schemas and error handling.
Create a safe SSRF design review using a mock URL-fetcher and allowlist test cases; do not target real internal services.
evidence_and_outputs: HTTP request/response captures with secrets redacted; endpoint inventory; auth matrix; reproducible test cases; remediation notes.
mastery_checks: Explain IDOR/BOLA vs authentication failure.
Show why an API gateway does not replace object-level authorization.
Identify safe validation for SSRF, injection and path traversal.
skills.safety: Use only explicitly authorised systems. Prefer local disposable labs, synthetic data, read-only validation and dry-run sinks. Do not reuse course credentials, secrets, target addresses or lab access details.

mastery_checks: Explain async vs sync I/O.

model_candidates.name: GPT-6 Astra
model_candidates.why: Official model documentation positions it for demanding reasoning, coding, computer use, research and multi-step professional workflows. The model page lists function calling, structured outputs, code interpreter, hosted shell, Skills, MCP and computer-use capabilities.
model_candidates.recommendation: Best first candidate for the main AI Red Teaming Agent, provided the account/API access, data handling and policy fit your engagement requirements. Use high reasoning for architecture analysis, attack-chain reasoning, code review and report synthesis.
model_candidates.caveat: Do not infer authorization to conduct live cyber operations from model capability. Verify current API availability, pricing, retention, data residency and safety conditions.

model_candidates.name: GPT-6-Cyber
model_candidates.why: The current OpenAI model catalog lists GPT-6-Cyber as a specialized cyber model for investigating vulnerabilities, reproducing them in authorized test environments and verifying fixes.
model_candidates.recommendation: Evaluate it as a specialist for authorized vulnerability research and validation if access is available to your account or organization.
model_candidates.caveat: Availability and eligibility may be restricted. Confirm access through official OpenAI channels; do not build the architecture assuming it is universally available.

model_candidates.name: Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Fable 5.1
model_candidates.why: Anthropic's current model documentation describes Opus for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work and Fable for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work.
model_candidates.recommendation: Use as an independent reviewer for code analysis, threat-model critique, test-plan review and cross-checking findings. Compare on your own benchmark before selecting.
model_candidates.caveat: Treat as a second opinion, not a source of truth. Validate tool permissions, data handling and model-specific safeguards.

model_candidates.name: Qwen family (select an appropriate current instruction/coding model)
model_candidates.why: The official Qwen model site describes a broad open foundation model family covering language, vision, code, math and reasoning, with multiple sizes and architectures.
model_candidates.recommendation: Consider for local/private inference, offline lab experiments, custom evaluation and privacy-sensitive workflows where you control hosting. Select a specific checkpoint only after reviewing its exact license, model card, benchmark and hardware requirements.
model_candidates.caveat: Open weights do not automatically mean secure, unbiased, safe, or suitable for commercial use. Verify license, provenance, vulnerabilities, quantization and tool-calling reliability.

model_candidates.name: Meta Llama family
model_candidates.why: Meta provides official model, hosting, integration and protection resources, and publishes model-specific license and use policies.
model_candidates.recommendation: Include a Llama checkpoint in the local-model bake-off if your hosting environment, license and application stack fit it.
model_candidates.caveat: Review the exact model version's license and acceptable-use terms; evaluate security behavior and tool calling independently.
